Modeling Stratospheric Plume Dynamics

Idealized simulations of a one-tonne SO₂ release across a ten-meter corridor. This model tracks dilution, aerosol microphysics, gas-phase chemistry, and photolysis rates until complete assimilation into ambient baseline levels.

The plume's movement across the globe is illustrative, not a simulation of stratospheric transport. Drift and shear follow a typical June wind so the plume has somewhere to live; the point is to show how dilution scales against the size of the Earth. Faithful transport would require running a global climate model.

Every curve on this page is output from a coupled chemistry, microphysics, and photolysis model of one plume; the day/night shading follows the model's own photolysis rates. Each case runs until the plume's surface area has stayed within 10% of the background for a full day.

For more information, the model architecture and documentation live on GitHub.
